terms.note: Tab name: the photo and video library. Also the plural of image in general. Feminine plural. Inside a sentence no article: em Imagens, de Imagens.
Singular in the setup texts: the downloadable system image written to the microSD card, not a photo. Feminine. Say imagem do sistema where it could be read as a photo.
Tab name: the people face recognition found. Also the generic word people, so not enforced.
Tab name. Groups of images are always called collections, in every app and on the site; never albums.
One group of images. Feminine; plural coleções.
Action in Images. Other texts quote it, so it is always these exact words.
Tab name: the folders and files on the device. Also the generic plural files. European Portuguese; never arquivos.
One file. Masculine; never arquivo.
A folder on the device or on a computer. Feminine.
Plural of folder.
Tab name: friends’ posts.
Tab name; also the generic plural.
One friend. The person’s gender is unknown: prefer the plural, the person’s name or a neutral wording. Amiga for a woman; with {name}, leave the word out.
Tab name: the device’s alerts and friends’ activity. Not the same word as notifications.
Tab name; also the phone’s own Settings app. European Portuguese (Brazil says Configurações). macOS: Definições do Sistema.
Menu heading above Social and Friends.
The Off The Cloud box (a Raspberry Pi with its disks) that holds everything; also the menu heading Device. Never server, NAS or box in app text. Masculine.
Plural of device.
Our relay at off-the.cloud that connects the apps and friends to a device away from home. A common noun, lowercase inside a sentence, one fixed word per language. Feminine: a ponte.
Being reachable through the bridge (a Settings section and the request a user account can carry).
Checkbox label quoted in other texts.
An account: the off-the.cloud account (bridge), a person’s account on the device (Settings, Users), or a Tailscale, Apple or Google account. Feminine.
Plural of account.
A person with an account on the device. Never usuário.
Plural of user; also the Users section in Settings.
The device’s owner: the person who set it up and manages its users.
The device password (it also unlocks the encryption) or an account password. European Portuguese; plural palavras-passe; never senha.
Plural of password.
One-time code from the off-the.cloud account page that links a new device to the account.
Plural of setup code.
Choice on the setup page and the account page; quoted on the site.
To set up a device the first time. The noun is setup. Noun: configuração.
Button on the welcome screens; quoted on the site.
Bring a device back from a disk taken out of it (recovery). Noun: recuperação.
Setup button; quoted in other texts and on the site.
Setup button next to Recover this device; quoted on the site.
Setup button that makes the device’s light flash; the apps quote it.
Space on the device’s disks; also the Storage line at the foot of the menu.
A storage disk or card plugged into the device.
The two disks kept as copies of each other (RAID 1). RAID itself is never translated. Mirrored: em espelho.
Keeping a folder the same in two places. Noun sincronização; synced sincronizado.
A folder synced in both directions (desktop apps).
A folder copied one way to the device (always upload only), and photo backup from the phones. Verb: fazer uma cópia de segurança.
Send a file from a phone or a computer to the device. Noun: carregamento.
Bring a file from the device to a phone or a computer. Noun: transferência. Never baixar.

A folder option: nothing in the folder can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps its older version. The name of the option, used as a label and inside sentences. Label Apenas carregamento; in a sentence: uma pasta em apenas carregamento.
Same option written as an adjective (an upload-only folder).
Folder action: its photos and videos are not tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them.
State of a folder after Keep out of Images. Worded without gender agreement on purpose.
Undoes Keep out of Images.

A link that lets anyone who has it download shared files until it expires (made with Share in Images and Files). Worded differently as a noun and as an action, so not enforced. Action: Partilhar ligação.
Settings section listing the share links and galleries.
A web page with copies of shared photos and videos, opened with a link.
Action in Images and Files; quoted in other texts.
A friends-only post in Social. English uses post as a noun and as a verb, so not enforced. Feminine. Verb: publicar.
Plural noun: friends’ posts.
Liking a post or a comment: the button, the count and the alert. English like is also a preposition, so not enforced. The button; the count is gostos. Alert: {name} gostou da tua publicação.
A comment on a post (noun and verb). Verb: comentar.
The text written with a post.
A request to become friends, between two devices.
Plural of friend request.
Accept a friend request.
Decline a friend request.
Block a friend.
Setting that finds faces so photos can be searched by person; runs on the device.
Setting that recognises what photos and videos show (a beach, a dog) so they can be searched; the result is tags.
The site’s name for image tagging; the same feature, so the same words.
Words found in a photo (beach, dog), shown as search chips. The tags themselves stay in English: they are search keys.
One tag (noun; to tag is not used in the apps). Feminine.
Settings action that runs tagging and face detection again on the whole library.

A file the device stopped processing because processing it kept failing (alert: <name> was set aside). Put the word file before the name so the participle agrees with it. O ficheiro {name} foi posto de parte.
Settings button that restarts the device.
A software update of the device or an app (noun and verb). Verb: atualizar.
An update the device should install soon.
Nothing to update.
Start a session with a password or with Apple or Google (web app, account page, setup). Button: Iniciar sessão.
End the session in this browser (web app). Button: Terminar sessão.
Phones: forget this device on this phone (connection and cache removed). Same words as sign out.
Mac and Windows/Linux apps: stop syncing with this device and remove its folders from the app.
Wireless network.
Older spelling in the setup page; same as Wi-Fi.
The network at home, where the apps connect straight to the device.
The network the device is on (addresses like 192.168.…).
The phone’s cellular data.
The Wi-Fi network the device opens during setup (named Off The Cloud).
The device’s address: a name under off-the.cloud or a ws:// address.
A name registered to the off-the.cloud account (name.off-the.cloud).
Push notifications on phones and in the browser.
The device’s log, in Settings, Logs; it can be sent to us for help. European spelling; never registros.
What friends see: name, picture and a line about the user.
The picture on the profile.
All the photos and videos on the device.
Small preview of a photo or video.
A photo. Images is the tab; inside sentences the apps say photos and videos. Feminine; fotografia in longer text.
A video. European Portuguese writes vídeo.
Plural of video.
A phone running the iPhone or Android app. European Portuguese; never celular.
Plural of phone.
A computer running the Mac or Windows/Linux app.
Plural of computer.
A screen of an app, or the device’s display. European Portuguese; never tela.
One of our apps: web, iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows/Linux. Feminine: a app; aplicação in longer text; never aplicativo.
The device’s own pages in a browser.
Mac app wording. The Windows/Linux app says this computer; the two apps’ texts are otherwise identical.
Windows/Linux app wording for this Mac.
Files are encrypted at rest with a key only the password unlocks.
An encryption key.
An older version of a file that the device keeps.
Both sides changed the same file; a copy of one version is kept.
The Raspberry Pi’s two blue USB ports; storage alerts say which one (top or bottom) holds the failed disk. A porta USB azul de cima / de baixo.
Action in Files; quoted on the site.
Phone photo-sync button; quoted in its explanation.
Phone photo-sync button; quoted in its explanation.
Logs button that sends the device’s logs to us; quoted elsewhere.
Button quoted in the onboarding texts.
Mac item that opens the app when the user logs in (the tray has the same item). Follows Apple’s Open at Login; check the wording on a Mac in that language.
Site wording: AI search, done on the device.
Site and account page prices.
Button.
Button; permanent removal. Apple says Apagar; Android and Windows say Eliminar. Never Excluir.
Button; takes something out of a list without deleting it.
Button. Never Compartilhar.
Button. Never Salvar.
Button that closes a finished screen. Apple says OK.
Button that acknowledges a message.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button in a sequence of steps.
Button.
Field placeholder and button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button. The sentence Try again. is in the language section. Sentence: Tenta novamente.
Button that postpones a question.
Button that grants a permission.
Switches a setting on (Turn Off: the opposite). Turn Off: Desativar.
Mac menu item: Quit Off The Cloud.
Sign-in button. Apple and Google publish the localized button titles; use theirs when they differ.
Sign-in button.
macOS settings app.
macOS and iOS settings pane.
iOS and macOS Control Centre.
macOS settings pane where login items are listed. Check the name on a Mac in that language before shipping.
macOS Trash, where the Mac app moves files deleted by a sync.
The Downloads folder.
Apple’s Photos app (not our Images tab).
The macOS menu bar.

forbidden.note: We address the user as tu.
Means delete in Brazil; say eliminar (delete) or manter fora (keep out).
